title: How Sleep Supports Teenagers
text:
Sleep supports how well teenagers function each day by affecting their brains, emotions, and bodies.

During sleep, the brain organizes information and prepares for the next day. When teenagers do not get enough sleep, memory, attention, problem-solving, and decision-making can suffer. Tired students may feel sluggish, make more mistakes, and find it harder to focus in school or while driving.

Sleep also affects emotional health. Poor sleep can make stress, anxiety, sadness, irritability, and frustration feel stronger. When people are rested, they are often better able to manage their reactions and cope with difficult feelings.

Physical health is affected as well. Sleep helps regulate hunger and appetite, supports healthier eating patterns, and gives the body time to repair itself. Not getting enough sleep can weaken the immune system and make it harder to fight illness. Getting sufficient sleep therefore supports teenagers' thinking, emotional balance, and physical health.
